Implementation Plan

Implementation plan: add `records_considered` to AI-memory retrieve output (Refs #8845)

Planning ref: `orchestrator/project-8845` at `ef9f747a1ac2c3db74c12989d378ee4298a808a0`. Integration branch mismatch: false.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends RetrievalResult
Scope-mode justification: The issue asks for one additive count, from the retrieve result through the CLI's JSON and `AI_MEMORY_TELEMETRY` output, plus tests and docs. The count already exists in `retrieve_memory_context`: the `scored` list (`scripts/ai_memory_lib.py` lines 2599-2618) is the set of eligible records after the status, prune, schema, category and scope filters and the record-id dedupe, before the budget loop. `miss_reason` already derives from it (line 2667). Reusing `len(scored)` needs no new pass over storage. The complete option (JSON and telemetry on all three CLI paths, plus tests for the over-budget, zero-hit, disabled and branch-unavailable paths) is only a few lines more than the shortcut. It moves correctness up under §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), so it is chosen. The read/commit/push timing split (`clone_ms` / `write_ms` / `push_ms`) is already on the ref and is not touched.

## Automation / scheduler impact (§20.E)
- No new script, supervisor or scheduler wiring. The change only edits existing code: `scripts/ai_memory.py` `cmd_retrieve` and `scripts/ai_memory_lib.py` `retrieve_memory_context`.
- Entry point: unchanged. Every workflow that already calls the retrieve wrapper in `scripts/memory_helpers.sh` gets the new field automatically.
- No database work, so no §20.D gate applies. No entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` is needed.

## Files likely to change
- `scripts/ai_memory_lib.py`
- `scripts/ai_memory.py`
- `tests/test_ai_memory_cli.py`
- `agents.d/wfopt-2026-10-02-memory-records-considered.md` (new)

## Functions or modules to implement
1. **`scripts/ai_memory_lib.py`, `RetrievalResult` (lines 128-136)**
   - Add `records_considered: int = 0` as the last field, after `selected_lesson_ids: tuple[str, ...] = ()`.
   - Existing positional and keyword construction stays valid, including `tests/test_orchestrator_completion_lessons.py` line 390, which only reads attributes.
2. **`scripts/ai_memory_lib.py`, `retrieve_memory_context` (lines 2525-2678)**
   - In the `return RetrievalResult(...)` call (lines 2669-2678), add `records_considered=len(scored),`.
   - Do not change the selection loop, the context text, `miss_reason` or any other field.
   - Add a one-line comment: the value is the eligible pool after the status, prune, schema, category, scope and dedupe filters, before the budget and `max_records` selection; lessons are counted separately.
3. **`scripts/ai_memory.py`, `cmd_retrieve`, disabled path (JSON at lines 217-225, telemetry at lines 227-234)**

4. **`scripts/ai_memory.py`, `cmd_retrieve`, branch-unavailable / git-error path (JSON at lines 262-271, telemetry at lines 273-281)**

5. **`scripts/ai_memory.py`, `cmd_retrieve`, success path (JSON at lines 322-335, telemetry at lines 337-348)**

   - `test_retrieve_reports_records_considered_above_records_selected`:
     - Write three candidates for one issue number. Give them distinct summaries and distinct `pr_number` values (None, 1, 2) so the record ids are unique, and check `len({ids}) == 3` as a precondition.
     - Run `retrieve --role implementation --issue-number <n> --max 1 --output-file <tmp>`.
     - Assert the JSON has `records_selected == 1` and `records_considered == 3`, with `records_considered >= records_selected`.
     - Assert the single `op == "retrieve"` telemetry entry carries the same two values.
     - Assert no record summary text appears in the telemetry line.
   - `test_retrieve_records_considered_zero_when_no_eligible_records`: empty stub store. Assert `records_considered == 0` in the JSON and telemetry, and `miss_reason == "no_eligible_records"`.
   - `test_retrieve_records_considered_zero_when_disabled`: set `AI_MEMORY_ENABLED="false"`. Assert the JSON and telemetry have `records_considered == 0` and `records_selected == 0`.
   - `test_retrieve_records_considered_zero_when_branch_unavailable`: patch `ai_memory.read_memory_root_from_branch` to raise `ai_memory_lib.MemoryGitError("couldn't find remote ref ai-memory")`. Assert exit code 0, `miss_reason == "branch_unavailable"` and `records_considered == 0` in the JSON and telemetry.
   - The direct-run `main()` picks the new tests up through its `test_` prefix scan, so it needs no edit.
7. **`agents.d/wfopt-2026-10-02-memory-records-considered.md` (new)**
   - One block under `<!-- agents: section="Workflow architecture" -->`. That section already holds the related AI-memory telemetry bullets ("Memory write phase timings (#8130)" at agents.md line 1684; `agents.d/8726-memory-push-retry-reasons.md` uses the same section).
   - One bullet: retrieve's JSON and `AI_MEMORY_TELEMETRY` now carry `records_considered`, which is `len(scored)` in `retrieve_memory_context` (the eligible pool after filters and dedupe, before the token-budget and `--max` selection), so it is always >= `records_selected`. It is `0` on the disabled, branch-unavailable and git-error paths. It is a count only. Tests: `tests/test_ai_memory_cli.py`.
8. **`changelog.d/wfopt-2026-10-02-memory-records-considered.md` (new)**

   - End with `Refs #8845`, a non-closing reference: #8845 is the orchestrator tracking issue (§21).

## Data structures affected
- `RetrievalResult` dataclass: gains the field `records_considered: int = 0`.
- Retrieve JSON on stdout: gains the key `records_considered` (int) on all three paths.
- `AI_MEMORY_TELEMETRY` line with `op=retrieve`: gains the key `records_considered` (int) on all three paths.
- No change to the context text written to `--output-file`, any memory record, any schema or the storage layout.

## API or interface changes
- The change is additive only. No key is renamed or removed (§10), and no CLI flag changes.
- Schema audit: no file in `ai-memory/schemas/` mentions `records_selected` or describes the retrieve JSON or telemetry payload. The schemas that use `additionalProperties: false` (memory_record, task_lineage, run_ledger_entry and others) are unrelated record shapes, so no schema edit is needed.
- Consumer audit:
  - Outside `tests/`, `records_selected` appears only in `scripts/ai_memory.py` and `scripts/ai_memory_lib.py`.
  - `AI_MEMORY_TELEMETRY` consumers (`scripts/summarize_unselected_runs.py`, `scripts/memory_helpers.sh`, the review scripts, `.github/workflows/workflow-log-analysis.yml`) parse the line as JSON and do not pin its key set.
  - No test asserts an exact key set for the retrieve payload; the `set(payload) ==` match is in an unrelated heal test.

## Decisions
### D1 — Use `len(scored)` as the candidate-pool size
- Chosen: `records_considered=len(scored)`, computed where `RetrievalResult` is built.
- Alternatives considered: `len(records)`, the pre-filter list that still includes schema-invalid, filtered-out and duplicate records; a new counting pass over storage.
- Why: `scored` is exactly the eligible pool after the existing status, category and scope filters and before budget selection, which is what the issue asks for. It is the list `miss_reason` already relies on, and it needs no extra I/O. `len()` on a list cannot raise, which meets the fail-open rule without a try/except.

### D2 — Do not add `records_considered` to the injected context text
- Chosen: JSON and telemetry only.
- Alternatives considered: adding a `records_considered: N` header line next to `records_selected:` in the context.
- Why: the issue scopes the field to JSON and telemetry. Changing the context text changes prompt bytes and token use for every role, and can break the context assertions in existing tests.

### D3 — Over-budget test uses `--max 1` on three eligible records
- Chosen: a deterministic record-count cap, through the existing `--max` flag (parser line 2380), which is applied in the same selection loop as the token budget.
- Alternatives considered: making enough long-summary records to exceed the 1,600-token budget of the implementation role.
- Why: the token estimate and summary-length validation make a token-overflow fixture fragile. `--max` reaches the same "more eligible records than the selection fits" condition with an exact expected count (3 considered, 1 selected).

### D4 — Docs go in an agents.d fragment under "Workflow architecture"
- Chosen: `<!-- agents: section="Workflow architecture" -->`.
- Alternatives considered: a new section; editing agents.md directly.
- Why: agents.md has no `##` heading devoted to AI-memory telemetry. The existing memory-telemetry bullets live in "Workflow architecture", and §25 forbids direct edits.
